subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue with the fixed 8192 MB managed-service default in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250, require a first-class heap-size tuning surface first, or switch to a Node CLI-argument shape to avoid generated NODE_OPTIONS?
rationale: The code fix is small, but the decision changes managed service startup defaults and needs maintainer ownership of low-memory-host behavior, operator overrides, and the intentional NODE_OPTIONS boundary.

options.title: Accept fixed default now
options.body: Land the narrow heap-only managed-service default as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require tunable surface
options.body: Pause the current fix until maintainers choose a config or CLI flag with upgrade and reinstall proof.

options.title: Use CLI argv shape
options.body: Prefer adding --max-old-space-size as a Node argv entry instead of generating NODE_OPTIONS, with repair/status consumers updated accordingly.

recommendation.title: Accept fixed default now
recommendation.body: Land the narrow heap-only managed-service default as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter's history covers the unified daemon install plan and daemon runtime best-practices surface that this product tradeoff affects.
